name: East Ridge
approach: From Trinity Trailhead, hike the Buck Creek Trail about 1.4 mi to the Chiwawa River Trail (#1550), then follow it north along the valley, passing beneath Red Mountain; leave the trail and climb cross-country to a bench near 6,300 ft, then traverse diagonally up toward Chiwawa Mountain's east ridge, descending to the roughly 7,200 ft col between Chiwawa and Fortress (or continuing over Chiwawa's summit first). Some parties instead approach via the Red Mountain Trail and Chiwawa Basin, fording the Chiwawa River. From the col, a loose class 3-4 gully gains the crest of Fortress's East Ridge.

approach_variants.name: Trinity and the Chiwawa River Trail to the Chiwawa-Fortress col
approach_variants.notes:
From Trinity Trailhead near 2,800 ft at the end of FR-6200, follow the Buck Creek and Chiwawa River trails up-valley beneath Red Mountain to about 6,580 ft, then leave the trail and traverse diagonally up toward Chiwawa Mountain's east ridge, descending to the roughly 7,200 ft col between Chiwawa and Fortress. Some parties go over Chiwawa's summit first instead. Others approach by way of the Red Mountain Trail and Chiwawa Basin, fording the Chiwawa River — the same basin the Chiwawa Mountain route uses, which puts you on the col from below rather than from along the ridge.

The col is a common high camp and this route is very often combined with Chiwawa Mountain from it, which is the practical reason to camp there rather than lower.

Rock quality is notably better on the East Ridge itself than in the gully that gains it or on Fortress's south-west face — the opposite of what most parties expect.

FR-6200 has been closed beyond Atkinson Flat, adding roughly seven miles of road-walking each way.
approach_variants.season: Jun-Oct. Crampons and an axe are commonly used on the snow slopes crossing to the col even in late summer
hazards: Loose rock in the gully gaining the East Ridge from the col — the worst ground on the route, and reversed on the way down
An exposed, normally unroped fourth-class step on the final summit pitch
Cold thigh- to knee-deep fords of the Chiwawa River drainage on the Chiwawa Basin approach
Steep firm snow crossing to the col, wanting crampons and an axe even late in the season
About seven extra miles of road-walking each way while FR-6200 is closed beyond Atkinson Flat
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The col is the camp and the gully is the route, and they are not the same place. From the roughly 7,200 ft Chiwawa-Fortress col, the East Ridge is gained by a loose class 3-4 gully. Standing on the col is not standing at the base; you still have a gully to find and climb before the ridge starts.

The rock itself is the confirmation, and it works backwards from what you would guess: the gully is the loose ground and the ridge above it is the solid ground. So the test that you have topped out of the correct gully onto the correct crest is that the rock gets better. If you have gained a crest and it is still rubble, you are on a subsidiary rib rather than the East Ridge.

The discriminator against the other route on this mountain: the south-west face is reached from an entirely different valley — Buck Creek Trail and Pass No Pass at about 6,400 ft — and never comes near this col. If your approach involved a way-trail and a pass rather than a cross-country traverse off the Chiwawa River Trail, you are on the other side of the peak.

The finish is one move and it is unprotected in practice: an exposed fourth-class step just below the summit, normally climbed unroped. That step is the route's crux and its arrival marker — reaching it means the ridge is behind you.

Coming back down, the head of the gully is the thing to find, and it is easier to walk past from above than from below. Follow the crest back until the ground drops away toward the col, and descend carefully; the gully is the loosest part of the day in both directions.

If you continue to Chiwawa Mountain from the col — which many parties do — note that its route works up the south-west side on slabs and talus from that same col, so the two climbs share a base and diverge immediately.

pitch_detail.notes: Buck Creek Trail to the Chiwawa River Trail at 1.4 mi. Stay left at the Red Mountain junction around 5 mi, where the faint branch drops to the valley, and ford the Chiwawa River. Faint paths and open forest lead to a basin near 5,500 ft, then a gully or treed slopes to the camp bench at about 6,300 ft. The upper trail is brushy with hidden deadfall.
pitch_detail.pitch: Trailhead to bench below Chiwawa's east ridge

pitch_detail.notes: From the bench, climb class 2 ground (a creek-side scramble works well in low water) to about 7,200 ft and traverse over to the flat col toward Chiwawa Mountain, which has wind-walled tent sites. A snowfield on the traverse toward Fortress can stay frozen hard into midsummer: carry an axe and traction, or drop below it rather than trying to skirt it high on loose rock.

Aim for the broad notch in the East Ridge, up moderate snow that steepens near the top or, late in the season, unpleasant choss and talus. The gully is very loose: scree slides underfoot, holds break, and parties above send down rock. The last stretch has narrow sandy ledges. At the notch, go left over blocks and loose talus to gain the crest.
pitch_detail.pitch: Col to East Ridge via gully

pitch_detail.notes: Stay as close to the crest as you can: the right side is very exposed and the left face is loose and sandy. The ridge rock is generally solid class 3–4, and a clean chimney through an otherwise blank block is the hardest move for many parties. Beyond it the ridge flattens into class 2 boulders and ledges to the true summit (8,674 ft), the farthest high point.
